cells.title: Record the tester's judge blocks inside a wave run
cells.verify: PATH="${CARGO_HOME:-$HOME/.cargo}/bin:$PATH" cargo test --release --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml --bin bee -- wave_run dispatch_wave

truths: after a test-role cell's herded run ends in a plain or rolling wave run, the runner reads that worker's report text and passes it to process_judge_from_text (verbs/cells/handlers_meta.rs) so each valid json <cell-id> block whose cell is one of the test cell's deps is recorded
a block naming a cell that is not a dep of the test cell records nothing; an invalid block records nothing and its error text appears on that cell's row
a code-role or docs-role cell's report is never read for judge blocks
each row carries capped (true or false, read from the cell store after the run) and judged (the list of cell ids whose verdict was recorded)
existing wave_run and dispatch wave tests pass, updated only where a row shape assertion breaks
must_haves.why: The opus leader paid several calls per cell between implementer result and cap (D1).

cells.action: Implement CONTEXT.md D1. In packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/verbs/drivers/wave_run.rs (run_wave line 107, run_rolling line 18, save_row line 68, row line 172) after each herding item finishes, read the cell from the store; if its role is test, read the worker report (the envelope saved by save_row names the job; the report sits in the job mailbox as report-N.md, find the reader herding already uses with rg -n report_path) and call crate::verbs::cells::process_judge_from_text for the blocks whose id is in the test cell's deps (filter the text to those blocks, or pass each block with its expected id). Add capped and judged fields to each row. Thread anything prepare.rs (run_dispatch_wave line 4668, rolling fill lines 4790-4840) must pass. Update only existing assertions that break; add no new tests (wct-5 owns them). Locate with rg -n and read ranges only. Write no code comment. Run only the cell verify, never the full suite. One commit with the cell trailer, files staged by explicit path. In your result put principles_used as an array of full slugs (bee-principle-<name> — <the decision it changed>), [] when none, and sync_ack with a reason if the cap sync door asks.

cells.title: Carry conflict verdicts the new cells do not touch
cells.verify: PATH="${CARGO_HOME:-$HOME/.cargo}/bin:$PATH" cargo test --release --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml --bin bee -- state_group plan_conflicts

truths: a derive stores beside the review a map from each plan cell id to a sha256 digest of its packet (the fields the terms and paths are drawn from)

a re-derive copies verdict and note from the previous review for each candidate whose id is unchanged, unless that candidate is also derived from the cells that are new or whose digest changed, and marks each copied row with carried_from set to the previous plan_rev
the first derive of a lane and a derive with no previous review carry nothing
the derive output line names how many verdicts were carried and how many candidates are open
existing state_group tests pass, updated only where an output text assertion breaks
must_haves.why: Adding 2 small cells reopened 62 candidates in token-spend-cuts (D2).

cells.action: Implement CONTEXT.md D2 in packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/verbs/state_group/plan_conflicts.rs. In run_plan_conflicts_derive (line 564, closure near 575-598) read the current conflict_review before building the new one. Compute a digest per plan cell (plan_cells line 121) from the fields plan_terms and plan_paths read. Find the new or changed cells against the stored digest map, derive candidates from those cells alone (factor derive_candidates_reported so it can take a cell subset), and copy verdict and note into every other new candidate whose id had a non-null verdict, adding carried_from. Store the digest map in conflict_review under cell_digests. Print carried and open counts on the derive line. Update only existing assertions that break; add no new tests (wct-5 owns them). Locate with rg -n and read ranges only. Write no code comment. Run only the cell verify, never the full suite. One commit with the cell trailer, files staged by explicit path. In your result put principles_used as an array of full slugs (bee-principle-<name> — <the decision it changed>), [] when none, and sync_ack with a reason if the cap sync door asks.

cells.title: List the read-only shell rules in the brief

truths: render_brief adds, only for a read-only job, a short Shell rules block that lists each command of READ_ONLY_ALLOWED read from worker_guard.rs (one source, no copied list) and names the refused forms: command substitution and backticks, redirects outside the job mailbox, sh -c and eval, sort, fd --exec, pipes into commands not on the list

a non-read-only brief is byte-identical to before
